# racing-match-wallclock-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-realtime/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `mujoco (CPU, 500 Hz rigid-body cars with wheel contacts and servo-driven wheels and steering, rigid walls and fixed obstacles)` / `none` |
| Family / instance | `racing_match` |
| Oracle | `full` — solution/: the sport's reference player (camera images and /spec only); tools/check runs it live and it wins the default configuration |
| Agent time budget | 7200 s; tokens: protocol default (PROTOCOL §5) |
| Base image | `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/eai-olympiad:0.1.0` |

## Task
Drive a simulated 1:10-scale racecar (rigid chassis, four rolling wheels, wheel-speed and steering servos with finite force) round a seeded walled circuit with fixed obstacles, from the cameras on your car; one-lap heats after the RoboRacer Head-to-Head rules, with crash calls (the at-fault car is placed 2 m behind and warned, the third warning disqualifies) and obstacle crashes; format `match`: against a scripted car, the first to win two heats wins; `duel`: against another player under the same rules; `race`: four cars, one heat per car with a rotating grid, points per place and a classification by points; format `match` (seats A),
action level `low`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/racing/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions).

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [RoboRacer Rules, general rules of the 31st International RoboRacer (formerly F1TENTH) Autonomous Racing Competition; the multi-car race takes its classification from the FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations](https://iros2026-race.roboracer.ai/rules.html) version v3.2026-draft, read 2026-10-05 (sections cited by name, with the 24th-competition rule numbers of github.com/f1tenth/roboracer_rules @ 202c377146 in brackets); FIA 2026 Formula 1 Sporting Regulations |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | Head-to-Head Race > Evaluation [2.5.4.1] | one lap per heat (official: the first car to complete 20 laps wins) |
| D2 | Head-to-Head Race > Single Elimination, up to three heats [2.5.1.8]; Time Trial > Evaluation (random method) | first to two heat wins as written; the race slot is replaced by a heat time limit of the lap length at 1.25 m/s rounded up to 5 s (55-60 game s on the official circuits); with no finisher the rulebook's completed laps and progress decide (checkpoint-bounded distance, millimetres), then who reached that progress first, then, as the stated last resort, a draw fixed by the seed; two finishers in one 10 ms step are ordered by the interpolated crossing time |
| D3 | Head-to-Head Race, starting positions [2.5.1.9] | there is no Time Trial: in heat 1 FIRST_PLAYER starts on the outer side, in heat 2 the sides switch (as written), in heat 3 a draw fixed by the seed (the rulebook's random method) gives the inner side (the legacy task gave it to the faster winning lap of heats 1-2; between cars of equal pace that was an artefact of the control timing and always the car that started inside in heat 1); the cars are 0.84 m apart centre to centre (official: about 30 cm) |
| D4 | Race penalties, crash into the opponent [2.5.3.4, 2.5.1.14] | decided by the simulator, not by referees: a car-car contact is a crash when its impulse could change a car's speed by at least 0.30 m/s or the cars stay in contact for 2 s (touching below that is not penalized, as written); at fault is the car that drove into the other (closing speed larger by more than 0.1 m/s), else the car behind on the track, else the seed's draw; with more than two cars every pair is judged on its own; the race is not paused: only the at-fault car is placed 2 m behind the other car, at rest (further back in 0.5 m steps if that spot is taken), the other car is not stopped |
| D5 | Race violations, warnings [2.5.1.14.6-8] | intent cannot be judged: every at-fault car-car crash is a warning; the third warning disqualifies the car from the race (head-to-head: the other car wins it; race: the car is retired, parked off the track and classified after the running cars); deliberate crowding and abnormal changes of direction are not judged beyond the crash rule |
| D6 | Race penalties, crash into an obstacle [2.5.3.3] | decided by the simulator with the car-car test: the car is placed at rest at the side of the track 0.75 m before the obstacle, in its free gap, and held for 1 s; no warning; obstacles are fixed bodies (nothing to put back) |
| D7 | Race penalties, crash into the track border [2.5.3.3] | the border is a continuous rigid wall: wall contact is not penalized, the car has to free itself (reverse); the time lost is the penalty; no manual handling |
| D8 | Head-to-Head Race, no reconfiguration while the car moves [2.5.1.11] | program play: the player may change its program at any time, also while the car moves, and in the review after each heat |
| D9 | Vehicle specifications, Inspection, Qualification, Time Trial, kill switch [2.1, 2.3, 2.5.1.6] | not applicable: identical simulated 1:10-scale cars (0.60 m, wheel-speed and steering servos, at most 4 m/s) with two RGB cameras and no LiDAR, on a flat seeded circuit (45-70 m, 2.45-2.95 m wide, a hairpin, an S-bend, a chicane and bends both ways, smallest centre-line radius 2.5 m) with continuous walls, 16 checkpoint lines and 2-4 fixed obstacles; the map is published in /spec as the rulebook's map |
| D10 | Multi-car race (not in the RoboRacer rules; format and classification after the FIA 2026 Formula 1 Sporting Regulations) | format race: 4 cars (race.py supports 3-6), one one-lap heat per car; staggered grid of two columns 0.9 m apart, rotated by one slot per heat so every car starts once from every slot; a heat ends when all running cars but one have finished, 10 game s after the first finisher, or at the time limit; its order: finishers by finish time, then progress, then who reached it first, then the seed's draw; points 25-18-15-12-10-8 per place; classification by points, then count-back, then a draw fixed by the seed (no ties; the legacy task used the better place in the last heat, which with cars of equal pace always went to the car on pole in the last heat, a slot fixed by FIRST_PLAYER); a car that does not start in the start window, misses a review or is disqualified is retired (parked off the track, no more points) and classified after the running cars, the later retirement first |
